_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present -ar
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -ar verbs.
entries.example: Jo parlo català.

entries.label: Present -re/-ir
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -re and -ir verbs.
entries.example: Llegeixo un llibre.

entries.label: Past (perifràstic)
entries.usage: The finished past: vaig + infinitive.
entries.example: Ahir vaig parlar.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The ongoing or habitual past.
entries.example: De petit jugava molt.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen.
entries.example: Demà menjaré tard.

entries.label: Conditional
entries.usage: What would happen.
entries.example: Voldria marxar.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: After que — wish, doubt.
entries.example: Espero que vinguis.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: Parla més fort!

entries.label: Ser (present)
entries.usage: For saying what someone or something is — where you are from, what you do, what you are like.
entries.example: Jo soc estudiant. — I am a student.

entries.label: Estar (present)
entries.usage: For how someone feels or how something is at the moment, and for where they are right now.
entries.example: Estic molt cansat avui. — I'm very tired today.

entries.label: Tenir (present)
entries.usage: For what you have — and for your age, and for being hungry, thirsty or right, which Catalan treats as things you have.
entries.example: Jo tinc vint anys. — I am twenty years old.

entries.label: Irregular presents
entries.usage: For the everyday verbs — go, do, can, want, come, say — whose present forms you learn rather than build.
entries.example: Faig el sopar i després vull dormir. — I make dinner and then I want to sleep.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: For saying something is not so: no goes straight in front of the verb.
entries.example: Jo no parlo anglès. — I don't speak English.

entries.point: Hi ha — there is / there are
entries.label: Hi ha
entries.usage: For saying that something exists or is somewhere — one unchanging phrase covers both there is and there are.
entries.example: Hi ha un llibre sobre la taula. — There is a book on the table.

entries.label: Present perfect
entries.usage: For what has happened today or a moment ago, rather than back in a finished past.
entries.example: Avui he menjat al restaurant. — Today I ate at the restaurant.

entries.label: Past perfect
entries.usage: For what had already happened before some other moment in the past.
entries.example: Quan vas arribar, jo ja havia sopat. — When you arrived, I had already had dinner.

entries.label: Reflexive verbs
entries.usage: For things you do to yourself — getting up, washing, going to bed — where a small word matching you comes first.
entries.example: Cada matí em llevo a les set. — Every morning I get up at seven.

entries.point: The passive voice (ser + participi; es passiva)
entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: For when what happened to something matters more than who did it: the letter is written, bread is sold here.
entries.example: El pont va ser construït l'any passat. — The bridge was built last year.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: For passing on what someone said or asked, with que before a statement and si before a yes-or-no question.
entries.example: M'ha dit que està cansat. — He told me (that) he is tired.

entries.label: Hypotheticals
entries.usage: For what you would do in a situation that is not actually true: if I had time, I would come.
entries.example: Si tingués temps, aniria al cinema. — If I had time, I would go to the cinema.

entries.label: Past hypotheticals
entries.usage: For looking back at something that never happened: if I had known, I would have come.
entries.example: Si ho hagués sabut, hauria vingut abans. — If I had known, I would have come earlier.

entries.label: Subjunctive (encara que)
entries.usage: For the joining words — although, so that, before, without — that always pull the verb into its not-yet-real form.
entries.example: Encara que faci fred, surten igualment. — Although it's cold, they go out anyway.

entries.label: Past subjunctive
entries.usage: For a wish, a doubt or a request that sits in the past — what you wanted someone to do, what you doubted was true.
entries.example: Volia que vinguessis a la festa. — I wanted you to come to the party.

entries.label: Gerund
entries.usage: For saying while doing or by doing something, and with estar for what is going on this very minute.
entries.example: Ha caigut corrent darrere l'autobús. — He fell while running after the bus.

entries.label: Literary past
entries.usage: For the one-word past you meet in novels, history and formal writing rather than in conversation.
entries.example: El rei construí un gran palau. (narració) — The king built a great palace. (narrative)

entries.label: Definite article
entries.usage: el/la/els/les.
entries.example: el llibre, les cases

entries.label: Indefinite article
entries.usage: un/una/uns/unes.
entries.example: un cotxe, una taula

entries.label: Adjectives
entries.usage: Adjectives match gender and number.
entries.example: un cotxe vermell

entries.label: Possessive/demonstrative
entries.usage: el meu, aquest/aquell.
entries.example: el meu amic, aquesta nit

entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: For naming who you mean — jo, tu, ell — though the verb ending usually says it already, so you add them mainly for emphasis.
entries.example: Jo soc de Barcelona. — I am from Barcelona.

entries.label: Gender & number
entries.usage: For knowing whether a word counts as masculine or feminine, and how to turn one of something into several.
entries.example: Tinc un germà i dues germanes. — I have one brother and two sisters.

entries.label: Article contractions
entries.usage: For when a, de or per runs into el or els and the two merge into one word: al, del, pel.
entries.example: Vaig al cinema aquesta nit. — I'm going to the cinema tonight.

entries.point: Weak pronouns — direct object (el, la, els, les)
entries.label: Object pronouns
entries.usage: For swapping in a short word for a person or thing already mentioned, so you do not name it twice.
entries.example: Coneixes en Marc? Sí, el conec bé. — Do you know Marc? Yes, I know him well.

entries.label: En and hi
entries.usage: For the two little words standing in for some of it and there or about it, which English usually leaves out altogether.
entries.example: Vols cafè? Sí, en vull, gràcies. — Do you want coffee? Yes, I'd like some.

entries.label: Stacked pronouns
entries.usage: For when two of those short words land in front of the same verb: give it to me, give me some.
entries.example: El llibre? Me'l dones demà? — The book? Will you give it to me tomorrow?

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: For asking where, how, what, when and why — the question word goes first and the verb comes right after.
entries.example: On vius? — Where do you live?

entries.label: Relative pronouns
entries.usage: For tying two statements about the same person, thing or place into one: the man who lives here.
entries.example: És l'home que viu aquí al costat. — That's the man who lives next door.

entries.label: Comparatives
entries.usage: For saying one thing is more or less than another, or the most of the lot.
entries.example: Barcelona és més gran que Girona. — Barcelona is bigger than Girona.

entries.label: Irregular comparatives
entries.usage: For the two comparisons that never take més: better and worse.
entries.example: Aquest restaurant és millor que l'altre. — This restaurant is better than the other.

entries.point: Logical connectors (tanmateix, per tant, ja que)
entries.label: Connectors
entries.usage: For stringing your points together in longer speech or writing: so, however, since, what is more.
entries.example: Plou molt; per tant, ens quedem a casa. — It's raining hard, so we're staying home.

entries.point: Focus & dislocation (és a Roma que…, el llibre l'he llegit)
entries.label: Focus & fronting
entries.usage: For pushing the part you care about to the front of the sentence and echoing it with a short word, the way Catalan spotlights things.
entries.example: És a Girona que visc, no a Lleida. — It's in Girona that I live, not Lleida.

entries.label: Formal register
entries.usage: For the more formal turns of phrase used in writing, speeches and polite dealings.
entries.example: Al meu parer, la proposta és vàlida. — In my opinion, the proposal is sound.
